title: My Purpose
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child explains Exodus 31:3 (God filled Bezalel with skill) and Romans 12:4 (one body, many parts with different work), says talents are God's gifts for serving others, and names values that grow them (practice, patience, discipline, humility).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parable of the talents.
floor.question: What did the faithful servants do with their talents?

representations: a body outline with parts labelled by job
steps: Name your gift and how it serves.
Name values that help it grow.
contexts: a learner who plays the drum in church

board.do: Draw a body and label hands, eyes and feet with their jobs.

board.say: What does Romans 12:4 teach with this picture?

board.do: Wait for the child to say many parts, different work, one body.

misconceptions.ask: Where do talents and abilities come from?
misconceptions.repair: Read Exodus 31:3: God filled Bezalel with skill. Ask the child to name a gift and say who gave it.
Link 1 Peter 4:10 with Romans 12:4: each part of the body works for the whole. Ask how a singer serves the church.

misconceptions.ask: Which verse says the body has many parts with different work?
misconceptions.repair: Give each verse a picture: Exodus 31:3, a craftsman; Romans 12:4, a body with many parts.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is a God-given talent?
misconceptions.repair: List gifts in the class; Bezalel's gift was craftwork (Exodus 31:3). Every gift serves.

checks.question: Where do talents come from, according to Exodus 31:3?
Name a value that helps a talent grow.
